The latest biweekly reading of the Penta-CivicScience Economic Sentiment Index (ESI) decreased 1.3 points to 31.0, reversing some of the gains from the previous period after the U.S. national debt was announced to have exceeded $40 trillion.

Four of the ESI’s five indicators decreased during this period. Confidence in the overall U.S. economy decreased the most, falling 3.0 points to 28.4. [...] —Confidence in buying a new home decreased 1.9 points to 24.4.  
—Confidence in finding a new job decreased 1.2 points to 27.8.  
—Confidence in personal finances decreased 0.8 points to 50.2.  
—Confidence in making a major purchase increased 0.4 points to 24.2.

results.content: That underlying debt caution becomes clearer with holiday shopping underway. With the backdrop of summer sales like Amazon Prime Day and Christmas in July, CivicScience data show 38% of holiday shoppers expect to spend more this holiday season. However, 48% of that higher-spending group also expect their debt to rise over the next six months, underscoring the need to track debt expectations alongside purchase intent for brands. results.content:
Amid a flurry of active food recalls, CivicScience data show 2 in 5 U.S. adults report having either purchased a recalled item or knowing someone who has, though notable differences exist across demographic groups. Forty-two percent of Gen Z respondents, aged 18-29, and 26% of urban respondents state that they have purchased a recalled product. In contrast, Baby Boomers (65+) and rural residents were the least likely, with 87% of those 65+ reporting no personal connection to the recent recalls. [...] © All rights reserved. CivicScience.
